extracted.intended_audience: general readers; improvisers and comedy students
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography of Del Close that documents his life, teaching, influence on modern improvisational theater, references (not a how-to), and mentions several comedic/improv techniques and practices associated with him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to create laughs (audience-first comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: There was an obligation to the audience to create laughs—not just to make them gasp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative principle for comic performance: prioritize generating laughter and audience engagement over merely shocking or eliciting gasps. Anti-pattern: using material that only shocks or horrifies without producing comedic payoff (example: Dave Thomas refused to enact a scene that he felt would only make the audience gasp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Horrifying honesty / radical personal honesty as a technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Close frequently used 'horrifying honesty' in performance and expected the same honesty from his actors ('Now perhaps you're not used to this particular kind of horrifying honesty, but I expect the same thing from you and nothing less').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: draw on extreme or candid personal material to fuel scenes and character choices. Guidance/ caveat: this approach can produce powerful, authentic comedy but is controversial and may cross ethical or taste boundaries; collaborators/audiences may object if it feels exploitative or fails to land as humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal/traumatic material as comic source
rubrics_metrics.description: Close frequently brought up his father's suicide in conversation and on stage, using personal traumatic history as material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice: incorporating real personal trauma can lend authenticity and emotional weight to improv material. Anti-patterns/risks: potential harm to performer or audience, ethical considerations, and the possibility that such use may not achieve comedic effect and instead alienate listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longform improvisation techniques (Truth in Comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book Truth in Comedy: The Manual of Improvisation (co-authored by Del Close) outlines techniques now common in longform improvisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: study and apply the methods described in Truth in Comedy to develop longform improv work; the book serves as a source of techniques and teaching practices used by many improv teachers and companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harold structure as a frame for longer improvisational scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth in Comedy describes the overall structure of 'Harold', which remains a common frame for longer improvisational scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: use the 'Harold' as a structural template for longform improv shows/scenes. Note: the article does not provide the Harold's steps, only that it is a widely used framework; further study (e.g., Truth in Comedy or other longform manuals) is required for implementation details.
